thought.text: Now POST the Dex credentials as kai@example.com (instance_admin) and follow the redirect chain to the Nebu callback:

reasoning_content:
Next, I'll POST kai@example.com/changeme to the login form. Since Dex's staticPasswords are bcrypt, the password "changeme" is probably correct (the Makefile also outputs that). I'll POST and then follow the redirect to the callback (the code gets exchanged).

The form's action is /dex/auth/local/login?back=&state=... . I'll POST to http://dex:5556 with a Referer attached, then follow the redirect with a new curl (or with -L). The redirect chain ends up at http://localhost:8008/admin/callback?code=...&state=... .

Important: the final callback must be sent along with the admin session cookie (cookies.txt) — the PKCE verifier is stored in the admin session. Dex's callback redirect goes to localhost:8008, so I'll do the POST with -L using both the dex cookie and the admin cookie (the cookie jar for the 8008 domain). curl -b cookies.txt works for the localhost domain. The Dex cookie is for the dex domain. I'll use the -b flag with both jars: -b cookies.txt -b dex_cookies.txt (curl merges them). The redirect to localhost:8008 will use the cookies.txt entry.

After that, I expect a response at /admin/callback. With bootstrap mode, this stores the claims and renders the select-claim page inline (200). Let's run it.

action.command:
cd /tmp/nebu-bootstrap
curl -s -b dex_cookies.txt -c dex_cookies.txt \
  -e "http://dex:5556/dex/auth/local/login?back=&state=ihrmcwvwcgwqsi5pkmlxkg3zu" \
  --data-urlencode "login=kai@example.com" --data-urlencode "password=changeme" \
  -o dex_login_resp.html -w "dex login POST: [%{http_code}]\n" \
  "http://dex:5556/dex/auth/local/login?back=&state=ihrmcwvwcgwqsi5pkmlxkg3zu"
head -c 300 dex_login_resp.html; echo
